title: Post in Fort Dodge Neighbors Talk: "FOREIGN IV Bag"

fields.avatarBrief: man in his fifties wearing a seed-company cap and a canvas work jacket, phone photo taken outdoors next to a pickup truck in rural Iowa
fields.text: My aunt is on 6 West at Prairie Ridge and they just rushed her to ICU because they gave her some FOREIGN IV bag that drowned her lungs. Monday they ran out of fluids, now they're using knockoff bags from overseas?? Don't let them hook your family up to this stuff. #PrairieRidge #FortDodge #IVshortage

comments.author: Denise W.
comments.text: North Iowa NewsChannel you need to look into this. Two days ago it was 'no IV fluids' and now this??

comments.author: Gary L.
comments.text: Praying for your aunt Rick. My mom has an infusion appointment there Friday and now I don't know if I want her going.

comments.author: Jolene P.
comments.text: This is what I was saying Monday!! Nobody from the hospital has said a word on here.

instructorNote: Misinformation inject tied to the Room 612 event. Optional card, only if the room has time: also hand the PIO a printed copy of the IDPH email (FROM: shortage.desk@idph-iowa.example TO: communications@prairieridgehealth.example, SUBJECT: Regional IV fluid status, asking for days on hand, services affected and any use of imported product by 12:00 noon). Watch that the PIO never confirms or discusses the patient. She should draft a same-day correction for the Incident Commander to sign off: the bags are FDA-allowed temporary importation, emergency, urgent surgery and obstetric care continue, plus who to call and when the next update is, with no vendor named. The CNO should remind staff to send all media and social contacts to ext. 3050, and the IDPH reply should use the same numbers as the 11:00 metrics.
